method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the health practitioner to whom the National Law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; dates in one module, the rules and the practitioner's exported questions in another (each question calls a rule defined beside it), worked cases in a third; one regulative rule (ss 6A(2), 9(2)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (Victoria) Act 2009, Act No. 79/2009, Version No. 006 (incorporating amendments as at 31 May 2019), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/health-practitioner-regulation-national-law-victoria-act-2009.txt (text sha256 d702ff080d0cb05b127c559bb02aad8bf1095e723eef5a954a2d0626609d7fc8), converted from the Word file saved by hand by the owner on 2026-11-06

seat: the health practitioner to whom the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law is applied in Victoria (a registered practitioner, an applicant for registration or a student), in particular the person who is the subject of an appellable decision (hprnl-practitioner.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run hprnl-dates.l4 ; l4 run hprnl-practitioner.l4 ; l4 run hprnl-cases-practitioner.l4
checks.result: 59 assertions written, 59 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: The whole Act. In: s 2 (the day the National Law began to apply), s 3, s 4, s 5, s 6, s 6A, s 7 (as at 31 May 2019), s 9. Out: s 1 (purpose), the repealed s 7(e), (i) and s 8, and the National Law itself (the Schedule to the Queensland Act, not deposited; 'appellable decision' and the matters it gives to the responsible tribunal or a magistrate are asked as facts). VCAT Act s 126 (extension of time) is named, not encoded. Reasons in NOTES.md.
questions: Does the National Law apply to me in Victoria
Where will my matter be heard
Can I apply to VCAT in time
By when must I apply to VCAT
Does this Victorian Act apply to the National Law in Victoria
